components.note: Definition complete (outcomes, events=2^Omega, mass function, induced P, complement, disjointness, support, null, almost sure); boundary: empty sum/product conventions, zero-mass outcomes kept in Omega, uniformity not implied by finiteness (51-55). Source variant preserved: GS Def. 1.2 calls the atom-weight function a "distribution function" (held PDF printed p.19) and line 51 records this.
All four items and the converse (existence and uniqueness of the inducing mass function) have written proof steps, including m=0 and Q(empty)=0 from pair additivity.
Random variable, events {X in D}, law, joint and marginal laws, f(X); boundary: zero-mass values and unattainable pairs (94-95).
Mass-function property, event formula, both marginals and the grouping formula for f(X) proved; empty fibers handled.
P(B)>0 hypothesis explicit; conditional measure and mass function; scope limit (defined update, not an unspecified process change).
Mass-function property, P(B|B)=1, transfer of identities, multiplication rule, chain rule with prefix-positivity hypothesis (final intersection may be null), successive conditioning; all proved.
Worked boundary: nonempty null event, 0/0 undefined, multiplication equation non-determining, no convention adopted, almost-sure event omitting outcomes.
Partition, priors, index set J excluding null hypotheses, likelihoods only for i in J, posterior with P(E)>0, odds with P(G)<1; likelihoods need not sum to one.
Total probability (both sums), Bayes with null branch, normalization, preservation of null hypotheses, odds form with q0>0 and 0<pi<1 (q1=0 covered); all proved without conditioning on null events.

Pairwise/mutual event independence, random-variable independence, conditional independence. GS Def. 4.2 (held PDF printed p.141) also states an equivalent complement form; the route preserves it at thm:p15-independence-basic item 2 and its agreement with the finite definitions (independent-random-variables.tex 84-89, 101-102).

Conditional criterion (P(B)>0), null events independent of every event, complement pairs, event criterion for variables (both directions), product construction; all proved. Preserves GS Def. 4.1 (conditional form with null clause, printed pp.139-140) and GS Thm 4.1 (product form).
Worked countercase: pairwise but not mutual independence, and conditioning on C destroying independence of A,B; numbers written.
Worked case: table, likelihood vs posterior, base-rate change, explicit two-alert product model with conditional independence, copied-alert countercase.
Expectation over outcomes, indicators, pointwise arithmetic, {X=Y}, f(X); finite sums so existence is automatic.

Grouping formula, E[1_A]=P(A), linearity incl. n=0 without independence, monotonicity, product rule under independence; all proved. Preserves GS Def. 6.1 / Thm 6.1 (value-sum form, printed pp.226, 230) via the grouping formula.
Worked boundary: linearity with coinciding summands; product of dependent indicators fails to factor.
E[X|B] for P(B)>0; E[X|Y]=g(Y) with chosen value on null fibers explicitly not a definition of null conditioning.
Partition averaging over J, averaging property on every D, E[E[X|Y]]=E[X], almost-sure uniqueness among h(Y); all proved; worked numeric check at 440-451.
Scope warning: model-dependence of numbers, no estimation/causation/prior selection/independence proof, LLN needed for empirical interpretation, enumerated omitted foundations.
